newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African truth body to hear child victims.
newsitem.headline: S.African truth body to hear child victims.

text.p: Children who were victims of a decade-long brutal turf war in South Africa's KwaZulu-Natal province will tell their stories to "truth commission" hearings next week, officials said on Wednesday.

The hearings in the east coast port city of Durban will focus on children traumatised in the political fighting between President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress (ANC), the Inkatha Freedom Party (IFP) and the apartheid security forces, commissioner Simangele Magwaza said.
The past decade has been marked by massacres of families, blamed on the ANC and Inkatha, who have been trying to build a stronghold in the province which is home to nine million Zulus.
"We know that especially in KwaZulu-Natal, with the nature of violence here, that very few children escaped that violence," Magwaza told a news conference.
"Our database reflects that very few children under the age of 14 were violated, and we know that is just not true. Children have been treated as an invisible group.
"With this hearing we want to highlight the fact that children suffered the same gross human rights violations as the adults did," Magwaza said.

She said originally Archbishop Desmond Tutu's Truth and Reconciliation Commission had planned to listen to the testimony of about 50 children eight years and older over three days, but the number had since grown.
Other children's hearings would also be held around the country later.
The commission, formed to probe human rights abuses committed by all sides during 30 years of apartheid rule in an attempt to cleanse old wounds, has focused mainly on adult victims.

Violence monitors have estimated that over 14,000 people have been killed since the mid-1980s and thousands more were forced to flee their homes in the bitter feuding between the two biggest parties in KwaZulu-Natal.
